identity.name: assert_lifecycle_phase_distribution
identity.description: Tier-3 CQA lifecycle distribution ASSERT (Spec 84 §3.4), run in the permits and coa chains right after classify_lifecycle_phase: the per-seq distribution of permits + CoA lifecycle_seq against the 110 universal_stream_catalog bands (one kind per seq — band_violation, no_band_configured, expected_data_missing — each routed to WARN or, under its operator posture flag, to a halting FAIL), the unclassified hard limit (halting), two drain-lag breakouts, the seq-unclassified count and three non-halting cross-status checks. Read-only: no write, no recovery, no counters (the ASSERT profile).

why_lock.text: Ported verbatim from the pre-conversion `const ADVISORY_LOCK_ID = 109` (scripts/quality/assert-lifecycle-phase-distribution.js:31-32, 03fcb569; Spec 47 §A.5), agreeing with src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts. Kept via identity.lock + the §5.4 source-text convention.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads the same memoized scan; a statement that throws (a missing universal_stream_catalog among them, ALPD-D4) means the distribution could not be measured, which must redden and stop the run rather than read healthy (Spec 30 §5.4.1). The pre-conversion step let the same errors escape pipeline.run().

why.text: An ASSERT declares counters none (Spec 132 §assert.1 R-CH), so records_total is the runner default. phase_distribution and seq_distribution ride as INFO context rows, seq_violations as the detail of seq_bands_warn / seq_bands_failing (R-EP); the unclassified count is its own check row. Consumer grep 2026-10-23: no reader of these records_meta keys outside the step and its tests (R-HR). Lock contention is the runner terminal lock_held_elsewhere (ALPD-D8); the halt message is the runner's "blocking checks failed: <ids>". audit_table.phase is the chain position (permits 21, coa 11; scripts/generate-sharing-phase.js) where legacy stamped the constant 22.

limitations.what: The bands are a snapshot calibration (migration 148: FLOOR(rows_count*0.7) .. CEIL(rows_count*1.3)+20 from the universal_stream_catalog rows_count snapshot). A seq whose real population drifts past its band reads WARN until an operator re-tunes it; the 33 catalog rows_count NULL/0 seqs carry no upper bound and read INFO whatever their count.

why.text: ALPD-D8: the generic runner emits the declared lock_held_elsewhere terminal on advisory-lock contention; the pre-conversion step emitted its own skipped summary with reason classifier_running (scripts/quality/assert-lifecycle-phase-distribution.js:911-928), although lock 109 is this step's own lock.

A WARN row stands (a per-seq WARN-routed violation, a drain-lag breakout, a cross-check below its FAIL tier) and nothing FAILED; selectTerminal picks this success terminal by the real status (the assert_coa_freshness form).

A check FAILED, so the row-derived verdict is FAIL and the runner stamps this terminal (scripts/lib/step/index.js: verdict FAIL with no accepted anomaly). Two exits share it: a NON-blocking FAIL (a cross check above its threshold) returns normally, so the chain continues and run-chain folds the step to completed_with_errors (C1 67663a81: a cross-check FAIL once skipped 10 downstream steps including backup_db); a BLOCKING FAIL (the unclassified hard limit, a promoted per-seq violation, an orphan band, an empty dead-status vocabulary) throws after the audit table is emitted, so the chain halts (the two C1 halting classes plus the two former refusals).

execution.on_check_error fail_step: a distribution statement threw (a missing universal_stream_catalog among them), so the distribution could not be measured ("I could not check" never reads as healthy, Spec 30 §5.4.1).
